questions.q: In h = W0 x + (α/r) B (A x), with W0 of size d × k, what are the shapes of B and A?
options: B is r × k and A is d × r
B is d × r and A is r × k
Both are d × k
B is r × r and A is d × k
questions.answer: B is d × r and A is r × k
questions.why: A takes the k inputs down to r numbers and B takes them back up to d outputs, so BA is d × k. In ComfyUI files B is lora_up with shape [out, r] and A is lora_down with shape [r, in].

questions.q: How many numbers does a rank-16 LoRA store for a 4096 × 4096 layer, and what share of the layer's 16,777,216 is that?
options: 131,072, which is about 0.8%
16,777,216, the same as the layer
questions.why: r · (d + k) = 16 · 8192 = 131,072, and the lab prints the ratio 0.0078.

questions.q: In the lab, the product of a 256 × 8 and an 8 × 256 matrix is a 256 × 256 matrix. How many nonzero singular values does it have, and why?
options: 256, because the result is 256 × 256
16, the sum of the two small dimensions
8, because a product cannot have rank above the inner dimension
2048, the number of entries in the small matrices
questions.answer: 8, because a product cannot have rank above the inner dimension
questions.why: Every column of BA is a combination of the 8 columns of B, so the rank is at most 8, and the lab counts exactly 8 singular values above 1e-10 of the largest.

questions.q: A LoRA file has no alpha tensor. What scale does ComfyUI's LoRAAdapter.calculate_weight use for it?
options: 1 / rank
0, so the LoRA is ignored
The rank itself
1.0, whatever the rank
questions.why: The code uses alpha / rank only when the file supplies alpha, and 1.0 otherwise. A new adapter made by Train LoRA gets alpha 1.0, so its scale is 1/rank.

questions.q: Why does the error fall from 0.6190 at rank 2 to 0.0192 at rank 4 for one target, but only slowly for the other?
options: The first target is rank 4 plus noise, so rank 4 covers it. The second is full rank and not compressible
Rank 4 trains faster than rank 2
The second target was trained for fewer steps
Rank 4 is a special value for every update
questions.answer: The first target is rank 4 plus noise, so rank 4 covers it. The second is full rank and not compressible
questions.why: The trained error matches the truncated SVD, the best any rank-r matrix can do, so the curve is set by the target. This is why LoRA needs the update to be low-rank, which the paper hypothesises for adaptation and the lab builds by hand.

questions.q: Base weights are stored in FP8 and a LoRA update 0.5% the size of the weights is merged and stored again. What did the lab find for rounding to nearest?
options: It kept all of the update
It kept 0.200 of the update, because 0.928 of the weights returned to the same 8-bit code
It kept 0.987 of the update, like bf16
It kept none of the update and raised an error
questions.answer: It kept 0.200 of the update, because 0.928 of the weights returned to the same 8-bit code
questions.why: The update is far smaller than the gap between FP8 values, so rounding sends most weights back where they were. Stochastic rounding, which ComfyUI uses for FP8, keeps the mean (1.005) but adds noise 3.36 times as large as the update.

questions.q: Which way does the standard Load LoRA node in ComfyUI apply a LoRA?
options: By weight patches: applied on every forward pass under dynamic VRAM, and under the older patcher merged into a module that fits or applied on each pass to one that does not
Always in bypass mode, to avoid touching the weights
By retraining the base model for a few steps
By editing the checkpoint file on disk
questions.answer: By weight patches: applied on every forward pass under dynamic VRAM, and under the older patcher merged into a module that fits or applied on each pass to one that does not
questions.why: LoraLoader calls load_lora_for_models, which registers patches. ModelPatcherDynamic.load attaches LowVramPatch objects, and the older ModelPatcher.load merges or attaches them per module. The bypass loader is a separate experimental node.
